final_candidates.decision_summary: Removes the predicted N459-Q460-T461 N-linked glycan sequon, likely relieving shielding of the receptor-binding surface and improving G-mediated entry.
Located within the NQT sequon; may alter local electrostatics or glycan occupancy and modestly tune entry without removing the N-linked site.
Removes the predicted N411-N412-T413 N-linked glycan sequon, likely reducing shielding near receptor-binding or fusion-relevant loops.

stop_reason.detail: No external evidence is available and further self-review is unlikely to change the current top-3 candidate ordering.

history.rationale: L96 lies in the G stalk domain; alanine substitution may destabilize the prefusion G-F interaction and thus increase F triggering. This could enhance cell-entry efficiency without disrupting receptor binding.
Stalk-proximal residue; alanine may subtly alter fusion triggering, but folding risk limits confidence.
I133 is in a stalk-proximal region likely involved in G/F functional coupling. Reducing side-chain bulk may lower the activation barrier for F triggering and improve fusion.
Membrane/stalk-proximal mutation could alter fusion triggering, but no direct evidence and possible destabilization.
N411 is part of a predicted N-linked glycosylation sequon (NNT). Removing this glycan by N411Q may expose membrane-proximal regions and enhance G-F fusion triggering.
Removes the predicted N411-N412-T413 glycan sequon, likely reducing shielding near receptor-binding or fusion-relevant loops.
E431 is a key ephrin-B2 contact residue. A conservative shortening to aspartate may subtly reshape the binding pocket and improve electrostatic complementarity.
Conservative negative-charge change likely neutral and least likely to improve entry; rejecting to make room for a more plausible glycan-removal candidate.

rejection.reason: Conservative negative-charge change likely neutral and least likely to improve entry; rejecting to make room for a more plausible glycan-removal candidate.

history.rationale: W434 is a central hydrophobic ephrin-contact residue. W434Y preserves aromaticity while reducing steric bulk, potentially improving fit for ephrin-B2 binding.
Conservative aromatic substitution in a surface loop may fine-tune receptor interaction without large structural cost.
E435 contributes to the ephrin-binding interface. Conservative substitution to aspartate may retain charge while altering geometry to strengthen receptor interaction.
Conservative charge-retaining change; low expected effect but less destabilizing than non-conservative alternatives.
Y438 is near the receptor-binding pocket. Removing the hydroxyl group by Y438F may increase hydrophobic packing with ephrin-B2 and stabilize the bound complex.
Removes a hydroxyl while preserving aromatic packing; may modestly alter receptor binding.
N459 lies in a predicted N-linked glycosylation sequon (NQT) adjacent to the critical Q460 ephrin-contact residue. N459Q should remove a large glycan shield and likely improve ephrin-B2 access.
Removing the predicted N459-Q460-T461 N-linked glycan sequon may expose the receptor-binding surface and improve G-mediated entry.
Q460 is a key ephrin-B2 contact residue. Replacement with arginine may add a longer positive side chain and form stronger electrostatic interactions with acidic ephrin residues.
Located in the NQT sequon; may alter local electrostatics or glycan occupancy and modestly improve entry without removing the N-linked site.
V139 is located near the stalk/head transition. Alanine substitution may increase local flexibility and promote the conformational change required for F activation.
Small hydrophobic change in a stalk-like region; possible fusion kinetics effect but weak rationale.
Removes the predicted N236-S237-T238 N-glycan; analogous glycan-shielding relief hypothesis to N459Q and N411Q, added at moderate confidence.
